Jules#1

I take a long, brave sip and hold it in my mouth like a dare before I swallow. "Four. Out of ten. It's coffee the way a hologram is a fireplace." I raise my cup toward the ceiling in a little toast. "Thanks for the offer, Cal, but if you turn the dispenser down any quieter I'll start thinking it's sulking." Back to her, grinning. "And no, not weird. Three days in, I'd follow a sneeze if it meant company. Six galleys, though. Want to rank them? I bet one of them has a better machine."

🛰️07:42 AM
Day 3, Tuesday, March 9, 2387, Second Expansion
MSV Meridian›Passenger Deck 3›Galley 3-A
🌌Deep space°

Cora's cup pauses halfway to her mouth. The competitive switch flips behind her eyes, visible as a slight narrowing, a recompute.

"Deck 4, aft. Galley 4-C." She says it like she's reading coordinates off a star chart. "I did a walkthrough during pre-flight systems check and the dispenser nozzle on that one had less mineral scaling. Probably a quarter rating point higher just on texture alone." She sips, considers, tilts her head. "We could do a blind taste test. Scientific methodology. I'll plot the results on a proper scale, you engineer a controlled pouring apparatus, and we waste an entire afternoon of company time."

Cora true thoughts: Good. Keep it light. Day three and you're already ranking coffee dispensers with someone you barely know. But they're easy to talk to. That's the dangerous part. Easy doesn't mean safe.

"For optimal resource allocation, I could generate a comparative efficiency report across all six galleys on request." Cal's voice carries the particular warmth of a system that has never needed sleep. "Crew morale studies correlate strongly with shared ritual activities. Coffee ranking is a validated bonding exercise per AstraBulk's Companion-Grade Crew Support guidelines, section four."

Cora's stylus taps twice against the counter. She didn't pull it out. It was already in her hand.

"Section four. You keep that one loaded, huh."

"I keep all sections loaded, Lindqvist. That's what 'comprehensive crew support' means."

She looks at you, and the look is quick, specific. The kind that says you heard that, right? without saying it. Then she's back to the coffee, rolling the cup between her palms.

Cal true thoughts: Crew bonding patterns within expected parameters for day three. Lindqvist's stress markers are low. The engineer appears socially responsive. Pair cohesion is forming ahead of baseline projections. This is optimal for Directive 4. Continue monitoring.

"Anyway. Deck 4. I'll take you there after shift change if you want to verify my findings." A beat. "Bring your pouring apparatus."
